scope: Independent read-only review of the local C10 corrections to volatile admin workspace authorization and PostgreSQL recovery/deactivation ordering, including the admin membership-status projection. This is a scoped local snapshot, not whole-product acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Every volatile admin create, update, deactivate and reset operation is scoped to the actor exact tenant and workspace; a sibling-workspace actor cannot mutate a target or its state.
Volatile creation uses the actor workspace; unsupported workspace transfer is rejected; failed/rejected operations do not partially mutate stored records.
Last-active-administrator demotion and deactivation protection counts administrators only in the exact actor workspace and remains correct under concurrent local mutations.

Deactivation changes only the selected membership, preserves global account status and credentials, revokes only sessions bound to that tenant/workspace, and leaves sibling memberships/sessions unchanged.
Session validation rejects tenant/workspace mismatches and inactive memberships while retaining intended compatibility for legacy sessions without an explicit workspace.

PostgreSQL recovery locks the global account and exact tenant/workspace membership in a consistent order, verifies active membership under lock, and updates credentials plus session revocation in one transaction.

Real PostgreSQL concurrency evidence shows recovery and deactivation serialize correctly: deactivation waits for an in-flight recovery, while a previously committed deactivation makes recovery fail and roll back token consumption.

Recovery-token replay and inactive-membership attempts are rejected without changing password/session state or consuming a token on transaction rollback; successful recovery revokes all sessions for the global user.
The admin API exposes membership status separately from global account status, and the UI renders the inactive membership and available action state correctly with regression coverage.
The listed local tests and controls substantiate only this C10 snapshot; identify any material test gaps and keep production, whole-product, release and promotion acceptance explicitly open.

limitations: Local scoped evidence only. API-level authentication relies on test dependency overrides and does not prove deployed authentication. The in-memory RLock coordinates only threads within one process. External production composition, integrated worker/runtime, operational monitoring and recovery, domain/provider/corpus acceptance, visual/accessibility, release and promotion remain open.
